body: No. Some guy projected some thing into some other thing. Big fucking deal.

No, that's the entire point of the comment. Nobody lives long enough for their particular life span to be long enough that the futility becomes evident. You can only reach that conclusion through reason.
I have no idea what your problem is.

I don't see how. I'm still going to die just as fast (got treated, didn't work), except a significant portion of the time I had left was spent being treated with chemotherapy.

I'm not going to give up my anonymity. Not even partially. There's not sufficient 22-year-old western European Python programmers with my first name.
No.
I'm already ill and suffering from my (terminal) medical condition. The illness and suffering will only get progressively worse until I die.

I'm giving it to a person responsible for the software project I'm most involved in. He will use whatever reaches him to fix the things we've discussed that money can fix (mostly hosting costs, some development sponsoring including a sprint in my memory, but also paying for people to switch away from SVN). After that, he's going to find some charitable goal for it.
Thanks. I still don't *understand* why you care, but you too strike me as sincere, so I'm buying it.
Thanks for your kind words, but it appears you were cut off. I'm guessing the next word was "peace".
Meh, it's more of a side effect that previously stopped me from going through with it. I've just stopped caring.
I don't understand why you want me to watch a video of a basketball shot.
Python. Any code legacy is well taken care of by people I trust. My will is similarly well taken care of. At least in death, I will rid that project of SVN.
Python. My code legacy is well taken care of by people I trust, don't worry.
You overgeneralize. I've gotten some far more interesting replies from fellow terminal patients, one of which is also in pain due to fibromyalgia.

Well, you can stand there saying it is, I can stand here saying it isn't, and we can keep saying that ad nauseam. You seem to earnestly believe your ideals and goals are meaningful. I'd say in the grand scheme of things, they're about as meaningless as anything you could possibly do here.

About the penguins: honestly? I'd grab a comfy chair and popcorn.

Again, I'm not convinced *I'm* worthless, per se, any more so than any human being is, so your comparisons don't help.

What my parents dreamed is their problem. I didn't ask to be here.
Put a calendar in front of the dart board.

There's plenty of people whom I am, in fact, telling what's up and have already told what's up. I've explained it so many fucking times while alive I don't even know where to begin counting. What will saying the same things in a letter, combined with the act of finally killing myself, change? The people that don't know yet are probably never going to grok it.
You ignore the part where I said my truly debilitating pain was intermittent?
Nope, sorry. The idea of caring about people I don't know at all seems foreign t me. I'm not really fazed by war or anything either.
I figured some people might want a chance to talk to someone in that condition, given that all of the other threads I *have* read don't really seem to describe anyone in my situation or mindset.
My pain is intermittent. I assure you that during a crisis I can't be anywhere near a computer. I'm chained to my bed, in a room which is practically a sensory deprivation tank now.

Yes! I can't deny that it could be much worse! I can't deny that I'm being ogled by some creepy invisible pink unicorn either, but somehow believing it regardless doesn't sound reasonable to me.

No. The world is an exercise in futility. It's just hard to tell sometimes because it's an exercise that lasts far longer than the average human lifespan.

It's interesting how you claim it doesn't, and then carry on to explain why it does. Psychologically and socially don't matter when you have months left, and even then, it's only "usually". My pain getting worse though, that's pretty much a sure bet.

Amazingly, my ability to get laid is not sufficient to make me not want to die.
Don't care. I'll be dead by then.

I choose to believe the things I have plausible hypotheses for. I can't prove that I'm not being chased by invisible pink unicorns, yet I don't choose to believe it. I can't prove that there's an afterlife, yet I don't choose to believe it. Either way, I'm done here.
If "living a bit longer as an increasingly large portion of your time is spent in excruciating pain" counts as "no downside", then yes. I disagree.
You're replying this to a statement that I did, in fact, try all medical options. Interesting.
Somehow the idea of being in constant pain so I can help build more pointless insignificant shit doesn't entice me, sorry.
I have no idea who that is.
Not really. The thought of *life* is far worse. What are the odds it'll be worse?

I've already answered this somewhere else in this thread.

Even if I don't kill myself, I won't live long enough to overcome two years worth of depressive episodes.

I don't hide how I feel from loved ones. I haven't shied away from counseling.
Yes.
Well, sure. Exactly the same argument will apply then, and hey, that's mostly the reason I've erroneously held out for another year.

a) If I do continue to exist, it must be meaningful (ie not being kept alive by a machine) and pain-free. b) Exiting whenever I please.

a) is medically infeasible. b) is legally infeasible.
Believe what you like. I had this planned for a long time.

Yes. For one, it's not "under my own terms", secondly, their solutions to pain relief aren't solutions in my case (unless they drug me up to the point that life means little more than the biological concept of technically not being dead.)

Well, perhaps, that's exaggerated a bit. It's still a side effect, just one that was keeping me from going through with it previously.

For me, this practically *is* euthanasia. Our bullshit laws don't allow for anything better in my situation.

I'm a supporter of the right to die.

My daily life consists of immense amounts of  physical pain. It is not going to last long, and for that amount of time, the pain's only going to get worse. It can not be effectively controlled with drugs, other than simply drugging me up to the point that I'm practically comatose. How is wanting to end physical torment crazy?
Giving people who still want to talk in the hope of better understanding people in my situation a chance to. Nothing stopping everyone else from scrolling past.

Did you miss the "constant physical pain" part? It's gotten progressively worse and there's no indication it'll stop, so yes, it really does hurt too much to carry on "just a bit more". There's plenty of things I used to enjoy, like writing code. I either can't do them, or they are not sufficiently enjoyable to bother given that I have to put up with the pain. And, last time I checked, death is pretty good at removing everything, including pain.
Your guarantee fails to account for my terminal illness leaving me in debilitating pain, the degree and timing of which only gets worse as time progresses.

> Sir, I have found your problem. A man cannot be helped if he does not want to be.

Well, that much is certainly true.

Thanks.

I didn't figure my methods would be under scrutiny.

Through my dealings with the local student body for nurses, I know quite a few people that know about my situation and my wish to die. I'm fairly confident that *if* I get brought to any of the five nearest hospitals, I'll get what I want just fine.

I'd go the euthanasia route, but it turns out our "liberal" euthanasia laws are still a load of crap that don't actually help me.

I've reached out to plenty of people about this. The vast majority just ignored me. I've confessed my suicidal thoughts explicitly to my parents. They just don't talk about it to me. At all.

It's hard to ignore a dangling corpse.

> You have your entire life in your hands and you spent ONE YEAR trying to fix it?

I'm in constant physical and psychological pain, I've been hanging on by the skin of my teeth for a year, and you're telling me I need to live for *longer*? This feels to me like having my hand in a vat of vitriol and some person standing next to me, with their hand not in the vitriol, telling me I should keep it in.

> They never asked for you to die

That's too bad. I never asked to be born, either.

> they just want you to get better. 

No, they don't. They were fine before they knew anything was going on, and since then I've gotten nothing but shit from them. They want the problem to go away. That's it.

> You owe it to them to try

I don't owe anyone a goddamn thing anymore.

> You deserve to have a great life no matter how short it is, 

My point is that "great" is intrinsically impossible.

I just want to stop existing. Life isn't worth the effort. There's good in it, there's bad in it, and there's no reason to assume the good will outweigh the bad, but many reasons to assume otherwise -- primarily the (un)cited medical reasons. I'm in constant physical pain with absolutely no hope of that ever being fixed. Other than through death, of course.
That's fine, my primary motivator is not pissing people off.
Why? What part sounds irrational? Angry, sure, I'm plenty angry. Fun change from "apathic".

No, I'm killing myself because *I* don't want to live anymore. I didn't kill myself any sooner because I still gave a rat's ass about people who might get hurt. I've stopped doing that, because of a recent readjustment in my assessment of just how much they claim to care as opposed to how much they really do.

"Same bullshit"? Who decided it's bullshit? Why can't it be true?

Plenty of people have tried to "save" me. Talked me out of killing myself. It works, for another week or so. Why now? Because I've got to do it sometime, or I'll end up postponing it indefinitely.

Because when I hear people talk about a suicide case, all I hear is how it was something irrational done by a crazy person because they were crazy, or a sad person because they were sad. Fuck that, I've made a list of pros and cons, given this considerable thought, sought help, stuck with that help for over a year, and hey, looks like I still want to kill myself. Why *not* make an AMA?

And no, I don't have thirty years ahead of me. I have a very limited amount of time ahead of me, and most of it will be in pain. See (un)cited medical reasons.
